title: Popup CRO: Corey Haines's playbook for popups that convert without annoying users
summary: An agent playbook for designing and optimizing popups, modals, slide-ins and banners. Covers trigger strategy (time, scroll, exit intent, click), popup types, copy formulas, frequency capping, accessibility, benchmarks, and A/B test ideas.

principles.text: Popup success depends on timing: show a helpful offer at the moment of need, not too early or too late.
principles.quote:
Too early = annoying interruption
- Too late = missed opportunity
- Right time = helpful offer at moment of need

principles.text: Prefer click-triggered popups; they have zero annoyance and convert far better because visitors self-select.
principles.quote:
User initiates (clicks button/link)
- Zero annoyance factor

principles.text: Avoid early time delays; wait 30-60 seconds or use scroll depth as a proof of engagement.
principles.quote:
**Not recommended**: "Show after 5 seconds"
- **Better**: "Show after 30-60 seconds" (proven engagement)

principles.text: Make popups easy to dismiss; a hidden close button makes users bounce entirely.
principles.quote: Keep visible (top right is convention) — users who can't find the close button will bounce entirely

principles.text: Write CTAs that are first-person, specific and value-focused rather than generic.
principles.quote: First person works: "Get My Discount" vs "Get Your Discount"

principles.text: Respect users with frequency caps, remembered dismissals, and exclusion of converted visitors.
principles.quote:
Show maximum once per session
- Remember dismissals (cookie/localStorage)
- 7-30 days before showing again
